sources.title: Exposure to Grocery Prices and Inflation Expectations
sources.authors: Francesco D'Acunto, Ulrike Malmendier, Juan Ospina, Michael Weber
sources.use: Purchase-frequency exposure and asymmetric salience of increases versus decreases
sources.boundary: US grocery scanner measures are not CE expenditure shares or diary purchase days

sources.title: The pass-through from inflation perceptions to inflation expectations
sources.authors: Stefanie J. Huber, Daria Minina, Tobias Schmidt
sources.use: Perceptions-expectations linkage and randomized information experiment
sources.boundary: German online-population survey; not an identified coefficient for US SCE

sources.title: Food prices matter most: sensitive household inflation expectations
sources.authors: Nikoleta Anesti, Vania Esady, Matthew Naylor
sources.version: BoE Staff Working Paper 1125, May 2025, originally published 2025-04-25
sources.use: Distinguish exposure from sensitivity; food and cross-group responses
sources.boundary: UK evidence, heterogeneous associations; not universal low-income response coefficients

sources.title: Learning from Inflation Experiences
sources.boundary: Does not establish a universal U-shaped age profile or permanently higher expectations of old people

sources.title: Subjective Models of the Macroeconomy: Evidence From Experts and Representative Samples
sources.authors: Peter Andre, Carlo Pizzinelli, Christopher Roth, Johannes Wohlfart
sources.use: Subjective transmission channels and randomized contextual priming
sources.boundary: Macroeconomic shock vignettes, not monthly SCE density responses; sample response fractions are not population assignment probabilities

sources.title: Indirect Consumer Inflation Expectations
sources.use: Demographic patterns can vary with measurement wording
sources.boundary: Indirect question differs from SCE Q9; no universal demographic offsets

sources.title: The Epidemiology of Macroeconomic Expectations
sources.use: Gradual propagation of expert/media information into household expectations
sources.boundary: Does not identify our respondents' networks or their individual update probability

sources.title: Sticky Information Versus Sticky Prices: A Proposal to Replace the New Keynesian Phillips Curve
sources.use: Infrequent information updating as a theoretical reference
sources.boundary: Price-setting model is not a direct empirical SCE household updating model
